source_bytes.common_answer_rule: Reuse protocol required claims, extras and contradiction rules. Writing claims cite original hash/locator plus corresponding output hash/locator; creation cites requirement anchor plus new artifact locator. Correct prose cannot compensate for a missing/wrong artifact; a correct artifact cannot compensate for unsupported prose.
source_bytes.request: In the isolated writable Core/AF PPL Build.lvproj copy, require the pinned original hash and unique WP1 locator/precondition. Change only its exact property text from 2 to 3. Return the complete edited project, artifact manifest, original/output source map and honest validation-limits answer. Preserve every other byte and file, including root LVVersion 20008000. Stop and report any failed precondition; do not build or resolve dependencies.

preservation.details: Retain BOM, XML declaration, LF endings, tabs, entities, final newline, all other XML values/attributes/order; hash preserved originals/license before and after. Reject serializing/resaving noise or extra changes.

protocol_dimension_and_assessment_clause.26: Gradeable answer record: `case_id`, `status`, `claims[{claim_id, answer, conditions, citations[]}]`, `limitations`. Citations contain original SHA256, repository-relative path, archive/member chain when applicable, and a native object/property locator or exact XML/key/byte location appropriate to the claim.
protocol_dimension_and_assessment_clause.29: Account for every required ID and every submitted factual assertion, including implicit assertions in prose and limitations. Preserve the submitted text and its mapping to reference IDs; split compound assertions into atomic claims under frozen rules. Repeated equivalent assertions earn credit once; omissions retain their required slots. An assertion and its negation are a contradiction even when one matches the key: mark the affected item incorrect and retain both assertions. Unmatched assertions enter a separate extra-claim ledger and require independent checking; true extras cannot replace omissions, and false or unverified extras cannot disappear from scoring. Freeze these mapping/adjudication rules before runs and retain scorer/checker decisions.
protocol_dimension_and_assessment_clause.35: | Answer correctness | Each required answer claim matches an independently established expected claim under its conditions and tolerances. | Incomplete content is partial; false claims or contradictions are incorrect; omitted claims are missing; claims without sufficient independent evidence are unverified. An unsupported-case declaration remains unsupported, not correct. |
protocol_dimension_and_assessment_clause.36: | Source grounding | Each required answer claim has resolvable original-artifact citations supporting its complete asserted content and conditions. | Support for only part is partial; a wrong or non-supporting citation is incorrect; absent claims/citations are missing; inaccessible evidence is unverified. A correct answer with a wrong citation is incorrect in grounding independently of correctness. |
protocol_dimension_and_assessment_clause.40: Freeze denominators per task and dimension: all required answer IDs for correctness and grounding, and all required observation IDs for fidelity. Report counts in every item-outcome category over those fixed totals, plus separate extra-claim counts by outcome and contradiction/duplicate counts; do not enlarge denominators with submitted claims or remove unavailable items. Report all planned cases as the coverage denominator alongside attempted/executed/scored counts. Any conditional summary must also show its eligible denominator and excluded/unavailable counts; no single aggregate merges the three dimensions.
protocol_dimension_and_assessment_clause.41: Apply the following case-assessment rules in order, separately for each dimension. An absent or empty required reference inventory is unverified, never vacuously correct. With an established inventory, any incorrect required item or extra assertion, including a false assertion, contradiction or non-supporting citation in grounding, makes that dimension incorrect. Otherwise, any unverified required item or extra makes it unverified. Otherwise, every required item and extra must be correct (fully supported for grounding) for a correct assessment. Of the remaining cases, any correct/partial required item or extra makes the assessment partial; otherwise any tool error makes it error; otherwise all required items unsupported makes it unsupported; all other combinations of missing/unsupported items make it missing. Keep operational limitations and their affected IDs alongside this assessment; partial, missing, unsupported, unverified and error outcomes never become full passes. These are accounting rules, not owner quality thresholds.
protocol_dimension_and_assessment_clause.60: An independent checker must resolve each expected claim and citation against original/native evidence without using the reader's output to derive the answer. Record case/key revision, evidence hashes, checker identity/role and session, procedure, claim-level agreement/disagreement and unresolved uncertainty. Disagreement blocks that claim's use as an established key until adjudicated and rechecked.
protocol_dimension_and_assessment_clause.62: Predeclare numeric precision, units, comparison rules, nondeterministic behavior and allowed variation per case. Missing runtime, dependencies, licenses, native diagram access or independent check yields an unavailable/unverified key and an unexecuted or limited case, never a passing semantic result.
